nodes.label: The logo
nodes.text: The logo

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.text: Concept The database (SQL) is the core every data career passes through (Excel → SQL → Python → Data Analyst / Data Engineer / Data Scientist). Following Grok's principle — the black hole is never drawn, only the light around it — the database is not drawn as a shape; it is the void at the centre of a disc of light. The void is the "unknown" that data science and AI explore; the three traced layers make it read instantly as a database.

nodes.label: Construction (viewBox `0 0 100 100`)
nodes.text: Construction (viewBox `0 0 100 100`) ```svg <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"> <circle class="disc" cx="50" cy="50" r="46" fill="#f4f4f4"/> <path class="void" d="M29 31C29 17 71 17 71 31V69C71 83 29 83 29 69Z" fill="#000"/> <g class="bands" fill="none" stroke="#f4f4f4" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"> <path d="M29 31C29 45 71 45 71 31"/> <!-- top rim --> <path d="M29 45C29 59 71 59 71 45"/> <!-- layer 1 --> <path d="M29 59C29 73 71 73 71 59"/> <!-- layer 2 --> </g> </svg> ``` Keep the class names (`disc`, `void`, `bands`) — the animation depends on them.

nodes.label: Usage rules
nodes.text: Usage rules - Default: white logo on black. Use `logo-light-bg.svg` only on light surfaces. - The void must always be the background colour (it is a hole, not a black shape). On a non-black background, use the inline version and set `--logo-bg` to that background. - Minimum size 16 px. Clear space around it = ¼ of its width. - No outlines, glows, gradients, rotation or added elements (stars, sparkles were tried and removed on purpose). - Wordmark: datafromzero, lowercase, Geist 500, letter-spacing −0.01em, to the right of the mark; tagline *From A1 to AI* in Geist Mono when space allows. ---

nodes.label: Logo animation (approved — match `logo-animation.mp4`)
nodes.text: Logo animation (approved — match `logo-animation.mp4`) Total ≈ 2.9 s. All in `logo/logo-animation.js`. | # | What happens | Duration / ease | |---|---|---| | 1 | A thin 1.2 px ring of light traces the circle, starting at 12 o'clock, clockwise | 1.1 s, `power2.inOut` | | 2 | The disc scales up from the centre and fills in; the trace fades out | 1.0 s, `expo.out` (overlap −0.15 s) | | 3 | The void (database) opens from the centre (scaleY 0→1, scaleX .7→1) | 1.0 s, `expo.out` (overlap −0.7 s) | | 4 | The three layer lines draw left→right, staggered | 0.6 s each, stagger .12, `power2.out` | - Plays once on homepage load. Tap/click the logo to replay. - `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` → no animation, logo shown static. - Nav logo: static, never animated. ---

nodes.label: Build notes for Astro Starlight
nodes.text: Build notes for Astro Starlight Priorities (in order): stability & speed → mobile-first (most readers are on phones) → nice motion. - Where GSAP is allowed: homepage and story / history / visualization pages only. Not on lessons, exercises or reference pages — those stay plain Starlight for speed. - Homepage: build it as a custom Astro page (its own layout, not the docs layout), port the prototype into components, and load GSAP only there (`<script>` inside the page/component so it is bundled per-page). - GSAP: `npm i gsap` (3.13+; all plugins are free now). Allowed: `ScrollTrigger`, `SplitText`, `DrawSVG` (SPEC D22). Use `gsap.matchMedia()` for reduced-motion and pointer checks, and kill ScrollTriggers on page leave if client-side navigation is enabled. - Starlight config: use `logo/logo-dark-bg.svg` as the site logo (with a light-theme variant `logo-light-bg.svg` if light mode is kept) and `logo/favicon.svg` as the favicon. Site name = placeholder. - Docs area look: apply the tokens in §2 (black background, Geist / Geist Mono) through Starlight's custom CSS so lessons and reference match the homepage. Two modes: - Study / lessons: open, quiet, one idea per screen, generous spacing. - Reference: book-like, indexed, searchable (Starlight's built-in search), compact. - Math: DS / Statistics pages need LaTeX — add `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` (and KaTeX CSS). - Fonts: self-host or use Google Fonts with `display=swap`; preload Geist 400. - Performance budget: homepage JS (GSAP + plugins + page code) ≈ 90 KB gzipped max (SPEC D22); no images required — everything is SVG/CSS. Content must be fully readable with JS disabled (GSAP sets hidden states, CSS never hides content by default — the prototype already works this way). ---

nodes.label: Quality gates
nodes.text: 6. Quality gates (SPEC §12): links validator, prerequisite-graph check, cspell, markdownlint, nbstripout check, Lighthouse CI, Dependabot (monthly, grouped). One build-time graph module (`src/lib/graph.ts`, CLRS ch. 20/22, run by `scripts/check-graph.ts` per SPEC §12): DFS cycle detection that prints the cycle path, topological-order check against `order`, reverse edges for a "Unlocks next" list in the lesson footer, and longest-path layering for the roadmap map. Zero runtime JS. Record "Unlocks next" (§5.1) and the roadmap map (§3.1 `/start/`) in SPEC when they are built. Then a small navigation PR: cross-document View Transitions (CSS, ≤150 ms, off for reduced motion) and Speculation Rule…

nodes.label: Story: depth-first search

nodes.label: No AI attribution anywhere
nodes.text: - No AI attribution anywhere. The owner is the sole author. Never add `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated with …`, session links, or any mention of Claude, Muse or other AI tools in commits, commit messages, PR titles/descriptions, issues, comments, code, docs or the changelog. Commits are authored as the owner (see git config). This overrides any default attribution.

nodes.label: No
nodes.text: - No accounts, saved progress, comments or in-browser code execution (SPEC §15).

nodes.label: Never break a published URL
nodes.text: - Never break a published URL. Topic slugs, no numbers, trailing slash. Renames need a redirect (SPEC §3.3).

nodes.label: Schemas are enforced
nodes.text: - Schemas are enforced with Zod content collections (SPEC §5). Missing required fields must fail the build.

nodes.label: Content portability
nodes.text: - Content portability: lessons are plain `.md`; use `.mdx` only for the components listed in SPEC §6. No other components or raw `<script>` in content.

nodes.label: Motion
nodes.text: - Motion: GSAP (`ScrollTrigger`, `SplitText`, `DrawSVG` only) on `/` and `/stories/*` only; homepage JS ≈ 90 KB gzipped max (SPEC D22). Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Every page must be readable with JavaScript disabled.

nodes.label: Speed first
nodes.text: - Speed first: lesson/reference pages ship no JS beyond Starlight's own. Lighthouse mobile ≥ 90 perf, ≥ 95 a11y.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.text: - Language: American English. Vietnamese lives under `/vi/` with the same slugs (SPEC §8).

nodes.label: Licenses
nodes.text: - Licenses: content CC BY 4.0, code MIT, datasets CC BY 4.0.

nodes.label: Analytics
nodes.text: - Analytics: Google Analytics 4 only after consent (Consent Mode v2 default denied) — SPEC §11.

nodes.label: Principles (in priority order)
nodes.text: Principles (in priority order) 1. Permanence. Every published URL keeps working forever. Content outlives the framework. 2. Stability & speed. Static site, minimal JavaScript, works with JS disabled, fast on a phone. 3. Academic quality. Versioned, citable (DOI), sourced, dated, reviewed. 4. Beginner-first. Audience knows only Microsoft Office; most read on phones. 5. Delight, sparingly. GSAP motion only on the homepage and story pages. ---

nodes.label: Design & motion
nodes.text: Design & motion - Tokens, typography and logo rules: see `design/README.md` §2–3. Dark is default; docs pages get a light toggle; `@media print` forces black-on-white, hides nav/buttons, prints link URLs. - GSAP is allowed only on `/` and `/stories/*`. Never on lessons, reference, datasets or project pages. - Every animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; all content is visible with JS disabled. - Study pages (lessons): wide line-height, max ~70ch, one idea per section. Reference pages: compact, scannable, fixed section order (§5.2). ---

nodes.label: Analytics & privacy
nodes.text: Analytics & privacy - Google Analytics 4, loaded only after consent (Consent Mode v2, default `denied`). - A minimal consent banner (Accept / Decline), choice remembered; "Cookie settings" link in the footer to change it. - Declining must leave the site fully functional; GA script must never block rendering. - `/privacy/` page states what is collected, why, retention, and how to opt out. - Events worth tracking (optional): `open_in_colab`, `open_in_sheets`, `show_solution`, `report_issue`. > Note: GA plus a banner costs some speed and simplicity; it was chosen for richer insight. > If the banner hurts the experience, GoatCounter (no cookies, no banner) is the drop-in fallback. ---

nodes.text: Quality gates (CI on every PR and on `main`) | Check | Tool | Blocks merge | |---|---|---| | Build + schema validation | `astro build` (Zod content collections) | Yes | | Internal links & anchors | `starlight-links-validator` | Yes | | Prerequisite / see-also ids exist; no cycles in prerequisites | `scripts/check-graph.ts` | Yes | | External links | `lychee` (weekly scheduled job, opens an issue) | No | | Spelling (American English) | `cspell` with project dictionary | Yes | | Markdown style | `markdownlint` | Yes | | Notebooks have no outputs | `nbstripout --verify` | Yes | | Accessibility + performance | Lighthouse CI on `/`, one lesson, one reference page | Yes if a budget is missed | Budgets: Lighthouse mobile ≥ 90 (performance), ≥ 95 (accessibility). Lesson pages ship no framework JS beyond Starlight's own. Homepage JS ≈ 90 KB gzip max (D22). Accessibility target: WCAG 2.2 AA (contrast, keyboard navigation, alt text, MathML). Maintenance: Dependabot monthly, grouped; Node LTS upgraded once a year; Astro/Starlight major upgrades only in their own PR with a full CI pass. `reviewed` dates older than 18 months are listed by a scheduled job. ---

nodes.label: Migration from `johnha912/data-odyssey`
nodes.text: Migration from `johnha912/data-odyssey` Decision (2026-11-15): build in the existing `datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io` repo and copy the content. 1. Copy the Markdown from `johnha912/data-odyssey` into `src/content/docs/` following §3, adding frontmatter (§5). 2. Record the source commit hash of `data-odyssey` in the commit message and in `CHANGELOG.md`. 3. Replace `data-odyssey`'s README with a short notice pointing to https://datafromzero.github.io, then archive that repo. 4. Tag the first public release `v1.0.0`, enable Zenodo, publish `CITATION.cff`.

nodes.label: Explicitly out of scope (for now)
nodes.text: Explicitly out of scope (for now) Accounts, saved progress, comments, in-browser code execution, paid content, newsletters, AI chat on the site. Each would need a new decision entry in §1 before being built.

nodes.label: Tech stack
nodes.text: Tech stack | Layer | Choice | Rule | |---|---|---| | Framework | Astro + Starlight (latest stable at build time) | Exact versions pinned in `package.json`; `package-lock.json` committed | | Runtime | Node.js current LTS | Pinned in `.nvmrc` and in CI | | Content | Markdown (`.md`) by default; `.mdx` only when a component from §6 is used | Keeps content portable to any future framework | | Schemas | Astro content collections + Zod | Build fails on invalid frontmatter | | Search | Starlight built-in (Pagefind) | Static, no external service | | Math | `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` (KaTeX, MathML output for accessibility) | Formulas in `$…$` / `$$…$$` | | Motion | GSAP 3.13+ (`ScrollTrigger`, `SplitText`, `DrawSVG` only) | Homepage and `/stories/` only (§10); homepage JS ≈ 90 KB gzipped max (D22) | | Hosting | GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions | Deploy on push to `main` | ---

nodes.label: Slug rules
nodes.text: Slug rules - Lowercase English, kebab-case, ASCII only: `/sql/window-functions/`. Vietnamese pages reuse the English slug. - No numbers, dates or versions in slugs. Order comes from `order` in frontmatter. - Always a trailing slash (`trailingSlash: 'always'`). - The slug is derived from the file name; the file name is the slug.

nodes.label: Change rules
nodes.text: Change rules - Never rename or delete a published URL. If a rename is unavoidable: 1. add an entry to `src/redirects.ts` (old → new), 2. keep the lesson `id` unchanged (§5.1), 3. note it in `CHANGELOG.md`. - A retired page stays online with `status: deprecated` and a link to its replacement. - Anchors (`#heading-id`) on reference pages are part of the contract — headings there are not renamed casually.

nodes.label: Linking inside content
nodes.text: Linking inside content - Internal links are root-relative (`/sql/joins/`), never absolute (`https://datafromzero.github.io/…`). - Link to other lessons by path; the build validates every internal link (§12). ---

nodes.label: Information architecture
nodes.text: Information architecture ``` datafromzero ├─ Learn (Study mode — open, quiet, one idea per screen) │ ├─ 1 Excel / Sheets → 2 SQL → 3 Python → 4 Advanced core │ └─ Branches: Data Analyst · Data Engineer · Data Scientist · Analytics Engineer · ML/AI Engineer ├─ Reference (Book mode — indexed, compact, searchable) │ ├─ Glossary │ ├─ Syntax: Excel functions · SQL keywords · pandas │ ├─ Statistics formulas │ └─ Careers (5 guides) ├─ Stories (history, explainers, visualizations — motion allowed) ├─ Datasets └─ About · Cite · Changelog · License · Privacy ``` Sidebar order and grouping are generated from frontmatter (`stage`, `order`), never hand-maintained. ---

nodes.label: Content model
nodes.text: Content model Schemas are registered in `src/content.config.ts` and defined in `src/lib/content-schemas.ts`; validation runs on every build (`src/lib/content-validation.ts`). Adding an optional field = MINOR change. Adding a required field, renaming or removing a field = MAJOR change + migration script. Rules for every type (D17): - `id` is lowercase kebab-case (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`) and unique across all content types (an English page and its Vietnamese translation share one id). - The file's folder decides its type (paths in the headings below). A file nested deeper than its type allows fails the build. - Every id reference must point to an existing entry of the right type. - `sources[].url` and `sheet` must be `http(s)` URLs. - The build reports all problems at once, naming the file and field, and fails.

nodes.label: Lesson (`src/content/docs/{stage}/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Lesson (`src/content/docs/{stage}/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: sql-joins # permanent internal key; never changes, even if the slug does title: Joining tables description: Combine rows from two tables with INNER and LEFT JOIN. # ≤ 160 chars, used for SEO/social stage: sql # excel | sql | python | core | data-analyst | data-engineer | # data-scientist | analytics-engineer | ml-engineer order: 40 # sort key inside the stage; use gaps of 10 so lessons can be inserted level: beginner # beginner | intermediate | advanced duration: 25 # minutes, integer objectives: # 2–5 items, each starts with a verb - Explain what a join key is - Write an INNER JOIN and a LEFT JOIN prerequisites: # lesson ids (not URLs); validated at build time - sql-select-basics datasets: [cafe-sales] # dataset names (§7); optional notebook: notebooks/sql/sql-joins.ipynb # optional; drives the "Open in Colab" button sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/…/copy # optional; Excel stage "Make a copy" link reviewed: 2026-11-15 # last date the content was checked for correctness sources: # at least 1; documentation, papers, books - title: PostgreSQL documentation — Joined tables url: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-table-expressions.html status: published # draft | published | deprecated replaced_by: null # lesson id, required when status = deprecated --- ``` - `stage` must match the lesson's folder. - `status: draft` lessons are built only in local dev, never deployed (D18). A published or deprecated lesson may not list a draft in `prerequisites` or `replaced_by`. - A deprecated lesson shows a notice linking to `replaced_by` (§3.3). Rendered at the top of every lesson: level · duration · last reviewed, then Objectives and Before this lesson (prerequisite links). Rendered at the bottom: Sources, Cite this lesson, Suggest an edit, Report an issue, prev/next.

nodes.label: Reference entry (`src/content/docs/reference/{area}/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Reference entry (`src/content/docs/reference/{area}/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: ref-sql-group-by title: GROUP BY area: sql # excel | sql | pandas | stats summary: Groups rows that share values so aggregates are computed per group. syntax: | # optional, shown in a code block at the top SELECT col, AGG(x) FROM t GROUP BY col; see_also: [ref-sql-having, glossary-aggregate] # ids used_in: [sql-aggregation] # lesson ids; optional (can also be computed) reviewed: 2026-11-15 sources: [ … ] --- ``` Reference pages use a fixed section order: Syntax → Parameters → Examples → Common mistakes → See also. `area` must match the folder. `see_also` is required (an empty list is allowed); its ids may be reference entries or glossary terms. `used_in` must name existing lessons that are not drafts (D18).

nodes.label: Glossary term (`src/content/docs/reference/glossary/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Glossary term (`src/content/docs/reference/glossary/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: glossary-primary-key term: Primary key short: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row. # ≤ 140 chars, used in hover/inline tooltips aliases: [PK] # required; an empty list is allowed reviewed: 2026-11-15 --- ``` `term` is also used as the page title.

nodes.label: Career guide, Story, Dataset
nodes.text: Career guide, Story, Dataset - Career (`/careers/{career}/`): `id`, `title`, `summary`, `skills[]`, `stages[]` (which stages/branches to finish), `reviewed`, `sources[]`. - Story (`/stories/{slug}/`): `id`, `title`, `description`, `published`, `reviewed`, `sources[]`, `motion: true|false`. - Dataset (`/datasets/{name}/`): files are defined in §7. Page frontmatter is not defined yet (D19); until it is, the build rejects dataset pages other than `datasets/index`. ---

nodes.label: Authoring components
nodes.text: Authoring components The only components content may use. Each must degrade to readable static HTML without JS. | Component | Purpose | No-JS fallback | |---|---|---| | `<Exercise id="sql-joins-1">` … `</Exercise>` | Numbered exercise block | Plain block | | `<Solution>` … `</Solution>` (inside `Exercise`) | Hidden answer, "Show solution" | Native `<details>` | | `<OpenInColab />` | Button from the lesson's `notebook` field | Plain link | | `<OpenInSheets />` | "Make a copy" button from the lesson's `sheet` field | Plain link | | `<Term id="glossary-primary-key">primary key</Term>` | Inline glossary link with short definition | Plain link | | Starlight `<Aside>` (note / tip / caution / danger) | Callouts | Built in | | `$…$`, `$$…$$` | Math (KaTeX) | MathML | Rules: - No other components or raw `<script>` in content. New components are added here first (MINOR change). - Components are available in every `.mdx` file without import lines (D21). The build fails, naming the file and line, on any `import`/`export` in content, any component not in this table, any `<script>`, event-handler attribute (`on…=`), `set:html` or `javascript:` URL (in `.md` or `.mdx`), a `Solution` outside an `Exercise`, or math inside a heading. - `Term` shows the definition as a native popover, with no JS: opened by hover/focus where interest invokers exist (`interestfor`), otherwise by a small "?" button next to the link (`popovertarget`, tap or click). Both dismiss with Esc or an outside click; the link always goes to the glossary page. - A literal dollar sign in prose must be written `\$`; otherwise `$…$` is read as math. - Exercise ids are permanent (`{lesson-id}-{n}`) so teachers can reference "Exercise sql-joins-2".

nodes.label: Future in-browser code (not now)
nodes.text: Future in-browser code (not now) Write runnable examples as fenced code blocks with a meta flag: ```` ```sql dataset=cafe-sales ````. They render as normal code today; a future `RunnableCode` enhancement (DuckDB-WASM / Pyodide) can pick them up without editing content. ---

nodes.label: Datasets
nodes.text: Datasets ``` datasets/ cafe-sales/ v1/ orders.csv customers.csv README.md # description, columns, types, row counts, how it was generated, license schema.yaml # machine-readable column definitions ``` - A small set of synthetic datasets the author creates, reused from Excel through Python so learners see the same data in every tool. No personal data. - Immutable once released. A change in columns or values = new folder `v2/`; `v1/` stays forever, so old notebooks and spreadsheets keep working. - Notebooks load data from a release-tag URL, not `main`: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/v1.0.0/datasets/cafe-sales/v1/orders.csv` - Each dataset also ships an `.xlsx` (Excel stage) and a `.sql` load script (SQL stage) generated by a script in `scripts/`. - License: CC BY 4.0. Notebooks: `notebooks/{stage}/{lesson-id}.ipynb`, opened via `https://colab.research.google.com/github/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/blob/main/notebooks/…`. Notebooks are cleared of outputs before commit (CI check). ---

nodes.label: Internationalization
nodes.text: Internationalization - Starlight i18n with `root` locale English and `vi` locale. UI strings translated in `src/content/i18n/vi.json`. - Vietnamese files mirror English paths: `src/content/docs/vi/sql/joins.md` with the same `id`. - Untranslated pages fall back to English with Starlight's "not yet translated" notice. - A translation records `translated_from_version` (curriculum version it was translated from) so stale translations can be listed. It is required on every Vietnamese page of a typed collection (§5), and the page must have an English counterpart at the mirrored path with the same `id`. - Code, SQL keywords and dataset column names stay in English in both languages. ---

nodes.label: Versioning, citation, changelog
nodes.text: Versioning, citation, changelog - Curriculum version (SemVer), tagged on GitHub as `vX.Y.Z`: - MAJOR — curriculum restructure, a required schema change, or any URL redirect batch - MINOR — new lessons, reference entries, datasets, components, optional fields - PATCH — corrections, clarifications, link fixes - Each GitHub Release is archived by Zenodo (GitHub integration) → one concept DOI (always latest) + one DOI per version. - `CITATION.cff` at repo root (title, author, version, date, concept DOI, license). Updated on every release. - `/cite/` page: APA + BibTeX for the whole work (concept DOI) and per-version DOIs. - Every lesson footer shows Cite this lesson: author, year (from `reviewed`), title, site, curriculum version, URL. Static pages cannot know when they were read, so a note asks the reader to add their access date (D20). - `CHANGELOG.md` follows *Keep a Changelog*; `/changelog/` renders it. - The site footer shows the current version and its DOI badge. ---

nodes.label: content-migrator
nodes.text: Moves and normalizes lesson Markdown - copies lessons from johnha912/data-odyssey, adds the required frontmatter (SPEC §5), converts links to root-relative paths, renames files to topic slugs. Use for build milestone 8 and for batches of content-format fixes. Does not write new lesson content.

nodes.label: frontend-designer
nodes.text: Visual and front-end work - design tokens, typography, theme toggle, print stylesheet, logo/favicon, porting the approved homepage prototype with GSAP (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, DrawSVG), story pages, accessibility and Lighthouse fixes. Use for build milestones 2 and 5 and any change to how the site looks or moves.

nodes.label: maintainer
nodes.text: Routine upkeep - verifies Dependabot/dependency bumps build cleanly, fixes typos and small wording or link errors, drafts issue triage, lists lessons whose `reviewed` date is older than 18 months (SPEC §12). Use for small, low-risk, well-defined chores; escalates anything else.

nodes.label: qa-runner
nodes.text: Runs the build and quality gates (npm ci, npm run build, npm run check, link check, Lighthouse) and reports only failures. Read-only - never edits. Use after every implementation step, before spec-reviewer, and for routine health checks.

nodes.label: site-builder
nodes.text: Implements site code - Astro/Starlight config, content collections and Zod schemas, authoring components, scripts, CI workflows and quality gates, project pages, bug fixes. Use for build milestones 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and any non-visual code change bigger than a few lines.

nodes.label: spec-reviewer
nodes.text: Reviews a finished change (diff) against SPEC.md CONTRACT sections, CLAUDE.md hard rules and the design handoff before it is committed or merged. Also consulted before any change to a CONTRACT or a SPEC §1 decision. Read-only. Use once per milestone/PR, after qa-runner reports a green build.

nodes.label: vi-translator
nodes.text: Translates English pages and UI strings into Vietnamese under src/content/docs/vi/ and src/content/i18n/vi.json, and lists stale translations. Use when English pages are ready to mirror, or to refresh translations after an English page changes.

nodes.label: astro.config.mjs
nodes.text: @ts-check https://astro.build/config SPEC §3.2: every URL ends with a trailing slash. SPEC §3.3: renamed URLs keep working through redirects. SPEC §2 / §6: formulas in $…$ and $$…$$, rendered to MathML only (no KaTeX CSS, fonts or JS). `unified()` keeps the remark/rehype pipeline that these plugins need. design/README.md §3: white mark on black by default, black mark on white for the light theme. The wordmark is the site title rendered beside the mark. Fonts are self-hosted (@fontsource) so no third-party request happens before consent. Code blocks follow the site theme only (never the OS scheme), on gray backgrounds. SPEC D9: dark by default, dark/light picker only. Lesson header and footer (SPEC §5.1); both render nothing on non-lesson pages. SPEC §8 / D3: English at the root, Vietnamese under /vi/ with the same slugs. SPEC §6: the six allowed components are available in every .mdx without import lines. order matters: Starlight first (its code-block integration must precede MDX), then auto-import, then MDX, because auto-import only hooks in when MDX is registered after it. Starlight enables MDX optimize when it registers MDX itself; keep the same output.

nodes.label: ActionLink
nodes.text: Shared button-styled link for OpenInColab / OpenInSheets. Internal: not exported to authors.

nodes.label: Exercise
nodes.text: SPEC §6: numbered exercise block. The id is permanent: `{lesson-id}-{n}`.

nodes.label: OpenInColab
nodes.text: SPEC §6/§7: button built from the lesson's `notebook` field; a plain link without CSS.

nodes.label: OpenInSheets
nodes.text: SPEC §6: "Make a copy" button built from the lesson's `sheet` field; a plain link without CSS.

nodes.label: Solution
nodes.text: SPEC §6: hidden answer. Native <details>, so it works without JS and by keyboard. Placement inside <Exercise> is enforced at build time by src/lib/remark-content-rules.ts.

nodes.label: Term
nodes.text: SPEC §6: inline glossary link. The short definition is a popover. Where interest invokers exist (Chromium) hover or keyboard focus on the link opens it (`interestfor`); elsewhere (Safari, Firefox) a small "?" button opens it by tap or click (`popovertarget`). Both dismiss with Esc or an outside click. No JS. The definition is also linked with aria-describedby. Unique per use, even when a term repeats on a page. Tap/click toggle for browsers without interest invokers. The 24 px target (WCAG 2.5.8) is built Anchored below the link by the browser; no gap, so the pointer can move onto the tip.

nodes.label: index.ts
nodes.text: The single import path for authors (SPEC §6): import { Exercise, Solution, Term, OpenInColab, OpenInSheets } from '~/components/content';

nodes.label: Branches
nodes.text: viewBox 0 0 1000 400: a trunk that forks at (500,130) into five branches (design/README.md §5).

nodes.label: Heading
nodes.text:
Heading copy: "\n" starts a new line, *text* is the muted second voice (design/README.md §2). split: words are wrapped at build time (hero only) so the CSS entrance needs no JS. The heading keeps one accessible name (aria-label) and the word spans are hidden from assistive tech. data-label carries the same name for the runtime splits (SplitText drops
when it builds its own). Other headings stay plain text; SplitText splits them in the browser when they near the viewport.

nodes.label: HomePage
nodes.text: The homepage for one language. All copy comes from src/i18n/home; links are language-aware.

nodes.label: Lines
nodes.text: Renders a string with "\n" line breaks.

nodes.label: Logo
nodes.text: The mark from design/logo/logo-inline-currentColor.svg, inlined so the void follows --logo-bg. Keep the class names (disc, void, bands): the animation depends on them. `animated` adds the thin trace ring and normalizes stroke lengths (pathLength=1) so the intro (design/README.md §4) can run as plain CSS keyframes, before any JavaScript is loaded. Accessible name. Omit for a decorative mark.

nodes.label: Marquee
nodes.text: Static and wrapped without JS or with reduced motion; the script turns it into a loop and shows the copy. Shown by the script only while the loop runs (WCAG 2.2.2); pauses on hover and keyboard focus too.

nodes.label: Nav
nodes.text: {t.github} ↗

nodes.label: LessonFooter
nodes.text: Rendered from frontmatter below the lesson content (SPEC §5.1, §9). No client-side JavaScript. A static page cannot know the reader's access date, so the citation omits it and the note says so. const repoUrl = `https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}`;

nodes.label: LessonHeader
nodes.text: Rendered from frontmatter above the lesson content (SPEC §5.1). No client-side JavaScript. Separator dots are drawn by ::before (2ch slot per item). The list is shifted left by one slot

nodes.label: Footer
nodes.text: Lesson footer (sources, citation, edit and issue links) above Starlight's own footer.

nodes.label: PageTitle
nodes.text: Starlight's title plus, on lesson pages, the lesson header (SPEC §5.1).

nodes.label: ThemeProvider
nodes.text: SPEC D9: dark unless the visitor has explicitly chosen light. Starlight's stock provider falls back to the OS color scheme; this one falls back to dark. Without JavaScript no data-theme is set and tokens.css already defaults to dark. {/* Inlined to avoid a flash of the wrong theme. */}

nodes.label: ThemeSelect
nodes.text: Dark / light picker. Replaces Starlight's three-way picker, whose "auto" option follows the OS color scheme; SPEC D9 makes dark the default instead. {/* Inlined to avoid a flash of the wrong value. */} Storage can be blocked; the choice then lasts for this page view only.

nodes.label: content.config.ts
nodes.text: SPEC §5: the content type follows the file path. Starlight's `docs` collection holds every page; the loader validates each file against its type's schema and checks cross-file rules (ids, prerequisites, translations). `extend` only carries the field types through to the page. UI strings: English in en.json, Vietnamese overrides in vi.json (SPEC §8).

nodes.label: index.ts
nodes.text: Prefix an internal path with the language root: /start/ -> /vi/start/ for Vietnamese.

nodes.label: types.ts
nodes.text: Copy for the homepage (/ and /vi/). One object per language, same shape (design/README.md §5). Text conventions: "\n" is a line break; *text* is the muted second voice of a heading.

nodes.label: HomeLayout
nodes.text: Own layout for / and /vi/ (not the docs layout). Always dark: it never reads or sets the docs theme. Fonts are self-hosted and Latin only here; Vietnamese files come with the /vi/ page (fonts-vi.css).

nodes.label: content-context.ts
nodes.text: Page context for authoring components (SPEC §6): which lesson / glossary term the page is, and the build-time errors for misuse. Throwing from a component fails the build. / Throws a build error naming the page and component. Next unused `{prefix}-{n}` for this page render (unique DOM ids). Remembers an Exercise id for this page render; false when it was already used on the page. SPEC §7: notebooks open from the `main` branch of the content repository. return `https://colab.research.google.com/github/${GITHUB_REPO}/blob/${GITHUB_BRANCH}/${notebook.replace(/^\/+/, '')}`;

nodes.label: content-schemas.ts
nodes.text: Zod schemas for every content type in SPEC §5 (CONTRACT). A page's content type follows its file path (see `classify`); project pages such as `start.md` use only Starlight's own fields. Adding an optional field is a MINOR change; anything else is MAJOR (SPEC §5). / Set on Vietnamese pages only (SPEC §8); presence is enforced in content-validation.ts. Locale prefix of the entry id: `vi` or null for English. Entry id without the locale prefix, e.g. `sql/joins`. The folder the frontmatter `stage` / `area` must equal. Set when a path inside a typed area is not a valid location. Maps a docs entry id (`sql/joins`, `vi/sql/joins`) to its content type. if (segs.length === 1) return none(); // stage landing page if (segs.length <= 2) return none(); // reference landing pages SPEC §5.4 / §7 define no dataset frontmatter yet (open owner decision): only index pages may exist. Starlight's `extend` schema: every typed field, all optional, so the validated frontmatter reaches the page unchanged. Real validation runs per content type in the loader (content-validation.ts). /

nodes.label: content-validation.ts
nodes.text: Build-time content validation (SPEC §5, §8). Wraps Starlight's docs loader: After loading, EVERY entry is validated against the schema for its content type and the cross-file rules are checked (unique ids, prerequisites, replacements, translations). All problems are collected and the build aborts once with the full list. / Glossary pages have `term`, not `title`; Starlight needs a title for the page. status: draft is excluded from production builds like Starlight's own `draft: true`. Keep going so every problem is reported together after loading. Astro only re-parses changed files, so validation runs here over every entry, every build. Per-file rules for every entry (schema, folder match, location, Vietnamese version). English pages own the ids. Ids are unique across all content types. see_also may point to reference entries and glossary terms only (SPEC §5.2).

nodes.label: lessons.ts
nodes.text: Lesson links for the given ids, in the reader's locale (`vi` pages link under /vi/). Prefer the translated title when the reader's locale has one; the URL is the same either way.

nodes.label: remark-content-rules.ts
nodes.text: Build-time rules for content: `<Solution>` is only valid inside `<Exercise>` (SPEC §6), and headings may not contain math. Runs on every `.md` and `.mdx` page before rendering; throwing here fails the build with the file path. / SPEC §6: the only components content may use. Auto-imported in astro.config.mjs. Imports injected by astro-auto-import have an empty value; anything an author wrote has source text. Script can also arrive through attributes: set:html, event handlers or javascript: URLs. if (name === null || name === undefined) return; // fragments are harmless

nodes.label: redirects.ts
nodes.text: Redirects for renamed URLs (SPEC §3.3). Published URLs are never removed: when a rename is unavoidable, add `'/old/path/': '/new/path/'` here, keep the lesson `id` unchanged and note the rename in CHANGELOG.md. /

nodes.label: home-boot.ts
nodes.text: First-load homepage script (about 1 KB). It never imports GSAP statically: the hero entrance is CSS, and the scroll choreography is fetched after the page has loaded (or on first interaction). Drop the reveal mask once the ripple has finished, so the grid is a plain layer again. Tap or click the hero logo to replay its intro. Restarting CSS animations needs one style flush. Motion is an enhancement: the page is already complete without it.

nodes.label: gsap.ts
nodes.text: Single entry to GSAP for the homepage. Imported only from the deferred motion chunks, so the library never sits on the critical path. Plugins are registered by the modules that use them. The mobile address bar resizing the viewport must not trigger a refresh while scrolling.

nodes.label: motion.ts
nodes.text: Deferred homepage motion: nav, scroll progress, hero scroll-out, pointer effects, and the lazy per-section timelines. Everything is inside gsap.matchMedia(), so reduced motion gets none of it (and in practice never even loads this chunk). Create a section's timelines only when it is within one viewport of the screen (one shared, code-split module). Scroll progress hairline: native scroll-driven CSS animation where supported, ScrollTrigger otherwise. Hero drifts away as the page scrolls (design/README.md §5): one scrubbed timeline. Nav: hides while reading down, returns on any upward scroll or keyboard focus. Section timelines, created on demand and code-split. Fonts change text metrics once: re-measure a single time. Pointer effects: fine pointers only (mouse and trackpad), never touch. The glow center eases toward the pointer; only style writes happen per frame. Measure once (document coordinates), refresh with ScrollTrigger; pointermove only reads event data. Magnetic buttons.

nodes.label: native.ts
nodes.text: True where CSS scroll-driven animations run the progress bar and rail fill (see home.css). Elsewhere the GSAP ScrollTrigger scrubs take over.

nodes.label: begin.ts
nodes.text: 04: the mark assembles (disc, void, layers), then the headline and button arrive, while the stage holds. 102%: Firefox can measure path length slightly short (see branches.ts)

nodes.label: branches.ts
nodes.text: DrawSVG end states use 102%: Firefox can measure path length slightly short and leave a gap at 100%. 02: one scrubbed timeline builds the tree while the sticky stage holds (CSS), or plays in flow on short screens. tl.to({}, { duration: 0.8 }); // hold the finished tree for a beat before the stage releases

nodes.label: core.ts
nodes.text: 01: each step lights up (and its counter ticks) as it is reached. The rail fill is a native scroll-driven CSS animation (home.css); GSAP scrubs it only as a fallback.

nodes.label: headings.ts
nodes.text: Word-by-word mask reveal. SplitText labels the heading for assistive tech (label restored from data-label). SplitText builds its label from textContent, which loses the line break: use the build-time one.

nodes.label: index.ts
nodes.text: One deferred module for every section timeline (a single request). Each section still initializes on its own, lazily, when motion.ts sees it within a viewport of the screen.

nodes.label: marquee.ts
nodes.text: Marquee: loops forever, runs only while visible, speeds up and leans with scroll velocity. WCAG 2.2.2: a visible Pause/Play toggle, and it also holds still while hovered or keyboard-focused. / Start deep into the repeats so scrolling up (negative timeScale) can run backwards without hitting time 0. onToggle only fires on changes: pick up the state at creation (the section may already be on screen). Resuming with the button focused must actually resume: ignore focus until it leaves. Only keyboard focus holds the loop (a mouse click on the toggle must not).

nodes.label: modes.ts
nodes.text: 03: panels wipe in from the bottom, their content rises, the progress pips grow. A slow counter-drift of the mock inside the panel gives the wipe some depth.

nodes.label: rules.ts
nodes.text: Section hairlines draw in from the left as they arrive.

nodes.label: yield.ts
nodes.text: Give the main thread back between chunks of setup work (scheduler.yield, with a timeout fallback).

nodes.label: site.ts
nodes.text: Single source of truth for the site name (design/README.md §7). Imported by astro.config.mjs and the pages; never hard-code the name elsewhere. export const SITE_URL = 'https://datafromzero.github.io'; GitHub repository that holds the content (edit and issue links). Curriculum version (SPEC §9); package.json `version` until releases are tagged.

nodes.label: fonts-vi.css
nodes.text: Vietnamese glyphs for /vi/ only; the English homepage never requests these files.

nodes.label: home.css
nodes.text: Homepage (/ and /vi/). Ported from design/homepage-prototype/index.html. Always dark. Nothing here hides content by default: the hero entrance is CSS keyframes that end visible, and every GSAP start state is set by script. Reduced motion and no-JS get the static page. / --ease: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); /* expo.out --ease-inout-quad: cubic-bezier(0.455, 0.03, 0.515, 0.955); /* power2.inOut --ease-out-quad: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94); /* power2.out { masked words (SplitText runtime masks, and the build-time hero words) progress + nav hero Dot grid: one container, two background layers. The lit layer follows the pointer through a opacity: 0; /* only visible while the intro draws it shared section padding: 0; /* the stage inside carries the padding 01 core: the label column stays put while the track scrolls (CSS sticky, no pinning) 02 branches 03 modes marquee: wrapped and static by default; a single looping line when motion is allowed Pause/Play toggle: shown by the script only while the loop runs 04 begin Sticky stages: with motion and script available, sections 02 and 04 become a tall wrapper with a viewport-high sticky stage, and a scrubbed timeline plays while the…

nodes.label: math.css
nodes.text: Math is rendered as MathML only (SPEC §2): no KaTeX CSS or fonts ship; the browser draws it. / Starlight's `:not(…) + :not(…)` flow spacing would otherwise hit MathML children (mi, mn, …). Display formulas: KaTeX emits <span class="katex"><math display="block">. Long ones scroll in their box.

nodes.label: print.css
nodes.text: Print: always light, black on white, no navigation chrome (SPEC D9, §10). Applies to docs pages; the homepage adds its own print rules in home.css. / Light tokens, whichever theme is on screen. Navigation chrome Content takes the whole page: remove the offsets that made room for the sidebar. Code: wrap, outline instead of fill. Syntax colors are tuned for a screen theme; print them black so they stay legible. Asides: outline instead of a filled box. Links read as text; external ones print their address. SPEC §10: print hides navigation and buttons.

nodes.label: tokens.css
nodes.text: Design tokens (design/README.md §2) mapped onto Starlight's custom properties. Black is the default theme (SPEC D9). The light theme is only reachable on docs pages through Starlight's theme picker, which sets <html data-theme="light">. The homepage never sets it. No gradients, no shadows, no color accents: everything below is a gray. / Raw tokens: the only values that change between themes. --bg: #000000; /* page background --fg: #f4f4f4; /* primary text, logo, solid buttons --mute: #777777; /* secondary text, mono labels, second line of headings --line: #1c1c1c; /* section dividers, hairlines --dim: #3a3a3a; /* inactive nodes / outlines The logo void is a hole: it must always equal the surface behind the mark. Light counterpart. --mute is darker than the dark theme's so it keeps 4.5:1 on white. Starlight mapping. Grays are derived from the raw tokens so both themes share one rule set. Hues are flattened to grays so asides, badges and cards carry no color accent. Typography Study pages: ~70 characters per line. Headings (design §2): weight 400, tracking -0.04 to -0.055em. Label style: Geist Mono 11px uppercase, tracked (section numbers, captions, mono labels). Wordmark: lowercase…
